'''Alexander Alexeyevich Makarov''', {{postnom|country=GBR|FRS}} ({{langx|ru|Александр Алексеевич Макаров}}; born 1966) is a Russian [[physicist]] who led the team that developed the [[Orbitrap]], a type of [[mass spectrometer]], and received the 2008 [[American Society for Mass Spectrometry]] Distinguished Contribution in Mass Spectrometry Award for this development.<ref>{{cite journal |author=Makarov A. |title=Electrostatic axially harmonic orbital trapping: A high-performance technique of mass analysis |journal=Analytical Chemistry |volume=72 |issue=6 |pages=1156–62 |year=2000 |doi=10.1021/ac991131p|pmid=10740853 }}</ref><ref name="ASMS">{{cite press release |publisher = Thermo Fisher Scientific |date = June 3, 2008| title = Dr. Alexander Makarov Receives 2008 ASMS Distinguished Contribution in Mass Spectrometry Award| url = http://www.thermo.com/com/cda/newsevents/news_detail/0,,20344,00.html?ca=ms| accessdate = October 20, 2009|url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090220174653/http://www.thermo.com/com/cda/newsevents/news_detail/0,,20344,00.html?ca=ms | archive-date = 20 February 2009}}</ref> In November 2013 he was appointed to Professor by Special Appointment of High Resolution Mass Spectrometry at the Department of Chemistry and the [[Bijvoet Center for Biomolecular Research]] of [[Utrecht University]] in the Netherlands.<ref name="UU">{{cite press release |publisher = Utrecht University |date = November 4, 2013| title = Alexander Makarov appointed as Professor of High Resolution Mass Spectrometry | url = http://www.uu.nl/faculty/science/EN/Current/Pages/Alexander-Makarov-appointed-as-professor-of-High-Resolution-Mass-Spectrometry.aspx| accessdate = November 5, 2013 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131105191459/http://www.uu.nl/faculty/science/EN/Current/Pages/Alexander-Makarov-appointed-as-professor-of-High-Resolution-Mass-Spectrometry.aspx | archive-date = 5 November 2013}}</ref>

As of 2016, he is Director of Global Research for Life Sciences Mass Spectrometry at [[Thermo Fisher Scientific]].

== Early life and education ==
* 1989 [[Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]] - M.S. Molecular Physics
* 1993 [[Moscow Engineering Physics Institute]] - Ph.D. Physics and Mathematics
* 1994-1996 [[Warwick University]] - Postdoctoral Appointment

== Awards ==
* 2008 [[American Society for Mass Spectrometry|ASMS]] Distinguished Contribution in Mass Spectrometry Award
* 2012 Thomson Medal Award
* 2020 [[Fellow of the Royal Society]]<ref name="frs">{{cite web |title=Fellow Detail Page: Alexander Makarov |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/Alexander-Makarov-25371/ |website=The Royal Society |access-date=12 May 2022}}</ref>
